answer: A routing exchange gives one dispatch slot to each key that books three live feeds for the same hour: a tide gauge for floods, a tundra probe for frozen roads and a dune sensor for sand drift. The exchange checks signed leases and rejects overlapping bookings on the same upstream channel, even through resellers. An honest dispatcher uses 3 channel-hours; 1,000 aliases need 3,000. At $3 per channel-hour, they spend $9 and $9,000 respectively, even if unused. This limits concurrent dispatch slots and assumes honest operators report channel IDs consistently.
